message:
Baraka, Chidi and Dalia, my part is only the solar electricity supply for the cold room.

Daytime supply can be covered by about four large panels. Following the divide daily use by peak sun hours rule in What Is an Off Grid Solar System? How It Works and What You Need (E1), an assumed eight kilowatt hour per day need at five peak sun hours needs about two point one three kilowatts, so four times five hundred fifty watt panels gives two point two kilowatts, using the LVTOPSUN 550W Solar Panel (E4) size of about two point two eight metres by one point one three metres. Four panels cover about ten square metres, about one parking space, plausible beside the room, under Sub-Saharan sun of four point five to six point five kilowatt hours per square metre per day in SOLAR IRRADIATION POTENTIAL OF AFRICA (E15).

Night running needs stored charge with a proper controller. The EG4 LifePower4 48V 5.12kWh 100Ah Lithium Iron Phosphate Battery (E10) provides five point one two kilowatt hours per forty eight volt one hundred ampere hour unit, where Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) means a long-life lithium chemistry, about half a household daily use, switched by the Victron BlueSolar MPPT 150/60-Tr Charge Controller - SCC010060200 (E7) rated at one hundred fifty volts and sixty amperes, where Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) means extracting peak panel power. I am not ready, because my eight kilowatt hour assumption needs Baraka's cooling load to fix array and battery size.
